name: Intibia Pivotal Study
question: Does active Intibia implantable tibial nerve stimulation improve urgency urinary incontinence outcomes compared with sham stimulation?

arms.label: Active Intibia implantable tibial nerve stimulation

design.population: 208 adults with urgency urinary incontinence despite conservative or behavioral treatment, including pharmacotherapy, were randomized after device implantation.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, sham-controlled randomized device trial
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Trial Design and Study Population; Results, participant disposition

verdictNote: The published QoL analysis omits the pivotal UUI responder results.
takeaway: Active Intibia implantable tibial nerve stimulation improved three-month patient-reported quality of life versus sham stimulation in a planned secondary analysis; the pivotal urgency-incontinence responder outcomes were reserved for a separate report.

reports.label: First published report: planned QoL analysis
reports.citation: Mangel J, Miller K, Erickson T, Dieter A, Roovers JP, Matthews CA. "Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Double-Blind Trial of the Intibia System in Urge Urinary Incontinence: Quality-of-Life Outcomes." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2026;37(10):3621-3630. doi:10.1007/s00192-026-06636-1
reports.followUp: Three-month blinded comparison; active-arm observations through 12 months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Trial Design; Tables 2-5

results.endpoint: PGI-I much or very much better
results.measure: Three-month patient-reported improvement; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Planned quality-of-life analysis; complete cases. The study's prespecified UUI responder endpoint is not reported here.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, PGI-I, three months

results.note: Complete cases; lower symptom-bother score indicates improvement.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, change from baseline MCID, three months

results.endpoint: OABq-SF health-related quality of life MCID
results.note: Complete cases; higher health-related quality-of-life score indicates improvement.
results.locator: Full text, Table 4, change from baseline MCID, three months

results.measure: Mean change from baseline at three months; mean difference in points
results.note: Between-group change did not differ statistically; complete cases.
results.locator: Full text, Table 5, ICIQ-UI SF change from baseline, three months

results.endpoint: OABq-SF symptom bother MCID at 12 months
results.measure: Active-arm improvement exceeding 10 points from baseline at 12 months
results.note: Within-arm observation after sham crossover and stimulation adjustment; no concurrent randomized comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, change from baseline MCID, 12 months

harms.label: Withdrawal owing to adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Results, participant disposition; Figure 1
harms.note: Seven of 208 randomized participants withdrew owing to adverse events across both assignments; event type and attribution were not reported in this QoL article.

delivery.label: Implant and stimulation schedule
delivery.value: All randomized participants received a subcutaneous generator with integrated subfascial lead adjacent to the tibial nerve; after two weeks, active stimulation was 20 Hz, 200 microseconds, 30 minutes daily for two weeks, then 30 minutes weekly.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Trial Design and Implant Procedure and Device Settings

delivery.label: Blinded period and crossover
delivery.value: The device remained off for two weeks after implantation; sham devices remained inactive until the three-month assessment, after which sham participants crossed over and stimulation could be adjusted.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Trial Design and Implant Procedure and Device Settings

delivery.label: Visit completion
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, participant disposition; Figure 1
delivery.note: The article prints 89.6% for 62/69 at 12 months; that fraction recalculates to 89.9%. Fractions are retained without percentages.
